What common student misconceptions or gaps in knowledge were seen in the responses to this 
question? 

Common Misconceptions/Knowledge Gaps 
Responses that Demonstrate Understanding  

 

 

• 
In part (a) responses were sometimes uncertain 
whether to use x = 2 or x = 3 to find the slope 
and/or equation of the tangent line. 

• 
Several responses made arithmetic mistakes when 
attempting to simplify tangent line approximations.

• 
In part (b) many responses began by using y = 1 in 
the given curve and found only x = + 43. Often 
responses that did solve and find both roots, 

x = ± 43, did not determine that the slope of the 
line through (−43, 1) was nonzero. 

• 
Some responses that found the points (± 43, 1) 
argued that the line y = 1 could not be tangent to the 
curve because “tangent lines cannot touch a graph 
twice.” 

• 
Several responses attempt to use only nonnumerical 
arguments to reason that the line y = 1 is not tangent 
to the curve. 

•

• 
In part (c) many responses included poor or incorrect 
communication. For example, many responses 
included the statements “the slope is vertical” or “the 
tangent line is undefined.” 

• 
Some responses began with a statement that in order 

for the tangent line to be vertical, dy

be undefined, but concluded with a statement that
